source_text.latin: 133 Propagatio pomorum ceterarumque arborum. Arboribus abs terra pulli qui nati erunt, eos in terram deprimito, extollito, uti radicem capere possint. 2 Inde, ubi tempus erit, effodito seritoque recte. Ficum, oleam, malum Punicum, mala strutea, cotonea aliaque mala omnia, laurum Cypriam, Delphicam, prunum, murtum coniugulum et murtum album et nigrum, nuces Abellanas, Praenestinas, platanum, haec omnia genera a capitibus propagari eximique ad hunc modum oportebit. 3 Quae diligentius seri voles, in calicibus seri oportet. In arboribus radices uti capiant, calicem pertusum sumito tibi aut quasillum; per eum ramulum trasserito; eum quasillum terra inpleto calcatoque, in arbore relinquito. Ubi bimum erit, ramum tenerum infra praecidito, cum quasillo serito. Eo modo quod vis genus arborum facere poteris uti radices bene habeant. 4 Item vitem in quasillum propagato terraque bene operito, anno post praecidito, cum qualo serito.
source_text.english: 133.1 To layer fruit and other trees: press back into the ground the scions which spring up from the ground, but raise their tips out, so that they will take root; dig up at the proper time and transplant vertically. In this way you should propagate from the crown and transplant fig, olive, pomegranate, quince, wild quince, and all other fruits, Cyprian and Delphic laurel, plum, conjuglan myrtle, as well as white and black myrtle, Abellan and Praenestine nuts, and plane trees. 133.3 Those which you wish to have planted more carefully should be planted in pots. To make them take root while on the tree, take a pot perforated at the bottom or a basket, run the shoot through it, fill the basket with earth, pack it, and leave it on the tree. When it is two years old cut off the tender branch below and plant along with the basket. By this method you can make any variety of tree take root firmly. 133.4 Vines may also be layered by thrusting them through a basket, packing firmly with earth, cutting a year later, and planting along with the basket.
source_text.english_scope_note: The online English page presents §133 in lines 32–34; line 33 contains the careful branch and line 34 the vine branch.

type_system.signature_conventions: OP nodes have fixed arity; SEQ and CONS are binary and NIL is nullary. Lists are never represented as opaque strings.

compiler_assumptions: SEQ is a serialization convention for preserving source order; it is not a claim about Cato's sentence boundaries.
CONS/NIL serialize every species-list member explicitly and preserve list order.
Reference identities connect pronouns only where the source text supplies a plausible grammatical referent; unresolved links remain explicit REFERENCE nodes.
The imperatives have an unspecified operator/addressee; no named owner or agent is inserted.
Purpose, capability, and conditional timing are distinct OPs. Purpose is not an observed result; capability is not a guarantee.
Ground-shoot branch has no invented age, basket, attachment, or cut. Its only timing is UNKNOWN proper time.
The pot/basket alternative, bimum antecedent, infra cut point, and qualus/quasillus identity remain unresolved.
Labels are source-analysis types, not Latin phonetic values or target word glosses.

uncertainties.text: Arboribus/abs terra and the English 'from the crown' do not license a universal ATTACH or PARENT predicate for the ground-shoot branch.
ubi tempus erit supplies a conditional proper time but no numeric age.
a capitibus may mean heads/crowns or another source-defined plant region; kept as a reference without choosing anatomy.
calix and quasillus are presented as alternatives, while later quasillus forms are written explicitly; the compiler retains both and does not unify all container references.
The two-year scope has no unambiguous grammatical antecedent in the compact AST; duration is attached to an unknown subject reference.
The lower cut reference is not measured or named.
qualus in §133.4 is not silently equated with quasillus.
mala strutea and murtum coniugulum are retained as source labels; their modern botanical identifications are not selected.

interface.tree_format: recursive arrays [OP_NAME, child1, ...]; operation children recurse as arrays and leaves are prefixed atom strings ref:, prop:, num:, or ent:.
interface.operator_type: OP_NAME is the first array element and is typed OP.
interface.list_convention: CONS(head,tail) is binary and NIL is nullary; species list is never an opaque string.
interface.sequence_convention: SEQ(left,right) is binary and preserves source order.
interface.source_ownership_field: source_ownership maps source spans to node identifiers and source propositions; node_trees provides each proposition tree.
